info.name: bpost API
info.description:
The bpost APIs, as the `webatvantage/bpost-api-library` PHP client calls them: the
Shipping Manager (orders and labels), the Geolocator (pick-up points, parcel points and
parcel lockers), and trackedmail (parcel announcement and tracking).

Built against the bpack integration manual v3.3.35 and bpost's own SHM API v5 example set.

## Credentials

Each service is a separate API with its own host and credentials — bpost issues them
separately, so holding one set does not mean you hold the others.

| Variable | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `accountId` | Your bpost account id. It is the HTTP Basic username *and* appears in every Shipping Manager URL; bpost checks the two match and answers 401 when they do not. |
| `shmPassphrase` | The Shipping Manager webservice password, from the Admin panel of the Shipping Manager backend — not your bpost portal login. |
| `parcelPassword` | Issued separately from the Shipping Manager passphrase. Request it from esolutions@bpost.be. |
| `geoPartner` | Your account id again, activated for the Geolocator. Sent as `Partner`, except on Get All Service Points where it is `Account`. |
| `geoApiKey` | The `x-api-key` bpost issues per account. Mandatory on every request to pudo.bpost.cloud since manual section B.4.1.0. |
| `geoAppId` | Optional four-character application id, used by bpost for statistics. |

Fill them in on the collection's **Variables** tab, or point the collection at an
environment holding the same names.

## Notes

- Every media type is versioned per operation, and bpost does not bump them in lockstep —
  a v5 operation can still answer a v3.4 media type. The Accept and Content-Type headers
  on each request are the ones that operation actually wants.
- The Geolocator reports failure in the body, not the status code: a
  `type="TaxipostLocatorError"` document comes back with HTTP 200.
- `deliveryDate` is set to today by a collection pre-request script, in bpost's `d-m-Y`
  format.
- An order reference or a barcode names one shipment rather than the account, so it is a
  **path variable** on the request that uses it — fill it in on that request's Params
  tab. The Geolocator passes its point id as the `Id` query parameter instead, since it
  has no path to bind.

exec: // bpost wants the expected delivery date as d-m-Y; keep it on today by default.

item.name: Shipping Manager — Orders
item.description: Orders live under `/{accountId}/orders`. An order is one reference and the parcels sent under it; a basket split across two parcels is one order with two boxes.

item.name: Create Order — home or office delivery

request.description:
Creates the order and its boxes. Posting an order whose reference already exists adds boxes to it rather than replacing it.

bpost answers 201 with an empty body and the order's location in a header.
